title: Modular exponentiation is polynomial-time computable
statement: For a bit string $z$, decode its first component $a$ and the two components $b,m$ obtained by decoding its second component again, using the empty word for any failed decoding. Interpret each bit string as a binary numeral, with the first bit least significant, and define the output to be the binary expansion of $0$ if the value of $m$ is $0$, and otherwise of $a^b$ modulo $m$. This function from bit strings to bit strings is polynomial-time computable.
